tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded session demonstrates logging in (already authenticated for tool use), selecting a parent category, opening Add Subcategory, filling Name/URL Key/Is Active/Include in Navigation Menu, clicking Save Category, and verifying the new node appears in the category tree.

Task Definition:
- Single purpose: create a subcategory under an existing parent category and set the basic attributes (name, url_key, is_active, include_in_menu). The tool uses the exact element hashes recorded where deterministic interactions were captured and uses an agentic selection step to locate the parent tree node by visible text (parent_name) because tree node element hashes vary by node.

Action Plan (ordered):
1) Navigate to category manager URL (deterministic URL recorded).
2) Find and click the parent node by visible text (agentic step since parent varies across runs).
3) Click Add Subcategory (deterministic elementHash recorded: 7616450bf1).
4) Wait for form render.
5) Fill Name and URL Key using recorded input element hashes (a075ffff62, 1914e4f18c).
6) Set Is Active and Include in Navigation Menu using recorded select element hashes (5208d8669b, 4f4efee99b) and visible option text (Yes/No).
7) Click Save Category using recorded Save elementHash (505367200f).
8) Wait and extract page content to verify success.

Variable Identification (tool inputs):
- parent_name (string, required): exact visible parent node label to target (user supplies 'Default Category' or others).
- name (string, required): the name of the new category.
- url_key (string, optional): friendly URL key (may be empty to auto-generate).
- is_active (string, optional): visible text 'Yes' or 'No' to set the Is Active field.
- include_in_menu (string, optional): visible text 'Yes' or 'No' to set inclusion in navigation.
- store_view (string, optional): store view scope; provided for completeness though the recorded flow did not change store view programmatically.

Step Optimization / Rationale:
- Prefer deterministic elementHash-based interactions for fields and buttons observed in the recorded successful session; these element_hash values point to single unique elements captured during recording and will be used for reliable clicks and inputs.
- The category tree node is dynamic (names and counts vary). Selecting a parent by visible text requires either a text-based XPath or agentic lookup; the recorded session used direct clicks on nodes by index so we implement an agent step to reliably find the visible link matching {parent_name} and click it. This avoids brittle text-only CSS selectors and handles variations in product counts.
- Kept waits short and deterministic after opening forms and after save to allow the UI to render and update messages.
- The tool intentionally focuses on creating subcategories (single purpose) because the recording included multiple related tasks (create root, update existing category). Creating a focused tool avoids conditional branching and keeps the flow deterministic and re-usable.

Notes and limitations:
- The session must be authenticated to admin (recording logged in as 'admin' earlier). This tool does not perform login; the session must already have admin access.
- If the Magento admin theme or markup differs significantly from the recording (different ids or missing elements), the agent selection step and the XPath in the verification step should be adapted. The tool uses elementHash fallbacks recorded in the session for the target instance shown.
- 'select_change' steps use visible option text 'Yes'/'No' (the exact visible text must be used). If your environment uses different locale labels, supply matching visible text values.
- The tool always attempts to set each provided attribute; if a parameter is omitted, the corresponding select_change will attempt to select an empty value which will have no effect in many browsers or may raise no-op — provide values for fields you want to set.

Deterministic selectors used from recorded session (elementHash references):
- Add Subcategory button: elementHash '7616450bf1'
- Name input: elementHash 'a075ffff62'
- URL Key input: elementHash '1914e4f18c'
- Is Active select: elementHash '5208d8669b'
- Include in Navigation Menu select: elementHash '4f4efee99b'
- Save Category button: elementHash '505367200f'

This tool follows the two-pass approach: PASS1 produced a deterministic sequence aligned with recorded actions; PASS2 optimization reduced UI steps by using recorded element hashes and an agentic parent-selection step instead of brittle text-only CSS selectors. The tool is single-purpose (create subcategory) which avoids conditional branching and keeps steps deterministic.
name: magento_create_subcategory_tool
description: Creates a subcategory under a specified parent category in Magento 1.x admin and sets basic attributes (name, URL key, Is Active, Include in Navigation Menu). Assumes the automation session is already authenticated to the Magento admin and landed on the Categories manager (http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_category/). Uses deterministic element hashes recorded during a successful session when available, and an agentic selection step to locate the parent category by visible text.

steps.description: Open the Magento admin category manager page (anchor URL used in the recorded session).

Parent category selection is dynamic (product counts change). Use agent reasoning to find the tree anchor text that matches the provided parent_name and click it to load that category in the edit pane.
steps.task: Locate and click the category tree node whose visible text contains '{parent_name}' and expand it so it is selected. If multiple matches, choose the one under 'Default Category' when possible.

steps.description: Click the 'Add Subcategory' button (recorded elementHash). This opens the New Subcategory form anchored to the selected parent.
Wait briefly for the subcategory form to render and for any JS to populate fields.
Enter the new category name into the Name input (recorded elementHash for the Name field).
Enter the URL Key into the URL Key input (recorded elementHash). If empty, Magento will generate one on save.

Set the 'Is Active' field by visible option text ('Yes'/'No'). Uses recorded elementHash for the Is Active select. If {is_active} is empty the field is not changed (the select_change will attempt to select the provided text; provide 'Yes' or 'No').
Set the 'Include in Navigation Menu' field by visible option text ('Yes'/'No') using the recorded elementHash. If empty the field is not changed.
Click the 'Save Category' button to persist the new subcategory (recorded Save button elementHash).
Wait briefly for the save to complete and for the admin to update the page/tree.
Extract key page content to verify creation: success message, tree node text for the new category, and edit-pane heading showing the created category ID.
steps.goal: Confirm the new subcategory '{name}' appears under '{parent_name}' in the category tree and that the success message 'The category has been saved.' is present.

input_schema.name: parent_name
input_schema.description: Exact visible text of the parent category in the tree (e.g. 'Default Category'). Used to locate the parent category under which the new subcategory will be created.

input_schema.name: name
input_schema.description: Name for the new subcategory (visible label). Example: 'Bot Subcategory Created by Tool'.

input_schema.name: url_key
input_schema.description: SEO-friendly URL key for the category (e.g. 'bot-subcategory-tool'). Leave empty to let Magento auto-generate.

input_schema.name: is_active
input_schema.description: Visible option to set the 'Is Active' field. Use the visible text exactly: 'Yes' or 'No'. If omitted, the page default will be used.

input_schema.name: include_in_menu
input_schema.description: Visible option to set 'Include in Navigation Menu'. Use visible text exactly: 'Yes' or 'No'. If omitted, page default is used.

input_schema.name: store_view
input_schema.description: Optional store view scope to select before editing (visible label in 'Choose Store View' dropdown). Example: 'All Store Views'. If omitted the current store view is not changed.
